story_markers: Provider scope story: {checks} live API assertions passed

requirements.expectation: Mock-admission loopback bootstrap: the story ensures the owner Human principal and a disjoint foreign Human principal exist through the loopback X-Mock-User-Id header before any business request; every later call carries the mock identity of exactly one of the two Humans.

The story registers one disposable Provider with static_bearer auth, a placeholder webhook_url and collaboration_scope standard; the response carries the provider_id and the provider_admin_token used by later admin calls.

Four provider Bots are minted through the provider admin token: one restricted-scope Bot owned by the owner, one Bot under a second standard-scope Provider owned by the owner, one restricted-scope Bot owned by the foreign Human (foreign scope), and later one owner-owned third Bot; each mint returns its bot_uuid.

The owner sets public visibility on its own two Bots and the foreign Human sets public visibility on its own foreign-scope Bot; each PUT /bots/{bot_uuid}/visibility succeeds for the minting owner only.

The standard-scope (cloud) Bot drives a public Group whose participants are the owner restricted-scope Bot and the owner Human (human_<owner>); group creation succeeds and returns the group id used by every later boundary exercise.

While the restricted policy protects the group membership, PATCHing the restricted Provider to collaboration_scope same_owner together with a rename is rejected 409 and leaves the Provider metadata unchanged: name stays the original and collaboration_scope stays standard.
PATCHing the Group to visibility private succeeds; the private transition itself is not the policy barrier for restricted Provider Bots.
The provider admin token promotes the restricted Provider to collaboration_scope same_owner, and the promoted scope is observable through the authenticated provider metadata read-back.

Once any restricted-scope Bot is attached to the Group, downgrading the restricted Provider back to collaboration_scope standard is rejected 403: the restricted policy is a one-way gate for attached Bots.
Under the current restricted policy the owner mints a third restricted Bot, sets it public and adds it as a member of the private Group; the restricted attachment path itself succeeds.
Adding the foreign-scope restricted Bot to the private Group is rejected 403: same_owner collaboration forbids cross-owner membership.
Creating a new Group driven by the owner restricted-scope Bot with the foreign-scope Bot as participant is rejected 403.
Creating a new Group driven by the foreign-scope restricted Bot with the owner Bot as participant is rejected 403.
Creating a public Group driven by the owner restricted-scope Bot with the standard-scope cloud Bot as participant is rejected 403: restricted Bots may not collaborate into public cross-scope Groups.
PATCHing the private Group back to public visibility is rejected 403 while restricted Provider Bots remain members.

The exact private-Bot collaboration requirement needs no friendship: setting the cloud Bot private, creating a Group driven by the owner Bot with the private cloud Bot as participant succeeds, and the cloud Bot is restored to public afterwards.
The invite-link surface mints an invite_token for the owner; the foreign Human joining through that link is rejected 403 while the owner Human joining through the same link succeeds.
Creating a chat Session on the Group returns 201 with a session_id for the owner, while the foreign Human creating a Session on the same Group is rejected 403.
Reading Session messages succeeds for the owner Human and is rejected 400 for the foreign Human: session-scoped reads carry the owner boundary.
Posting a chat message to the owner Session as the foreign Human is rejected 403 before any delivery occurs.

The Workbench WebSocket answers the 101 Switching Protocols upgrade and the exact connect request projection respects the owner boundary: the owner Human connect converges ok=true and the foreign Human connect converges ok=false.

Removing all restricted Bots from the Group membership restores legacy behavior without a permanent group policy: the visibility patch to public succeeds, the foreign Human joins through the earlier invite link, reads the Session messages and converges its Workbench connect to ok=true.
Re-adding the owner restricted-scope Bot to the restored legacy Group is still rejected 403, and the story prints the frozen live-API assertion count marker.

Teardown deletes both Groups through the bot_id query of their respective drivers and deletes every minted provider Bot through the provider admin token; any cleanup failure fails the whole story instead of leaking provider state.

documented_gaps.PREPROD_PROVIDER_ADMIN_FACE_ABSENT: The preprod faces expose group.* and session.* routes only (profiles/preprod.example.json route_bindings and the live preprod profile); the Provider registration/admin surface (/providers, /providers/{provider_id}/bots) is a BCS-internal face authenticated by the provider_admin_token bearer and admitted through loopback X-Mock-User-Id headers, neither of which exists on the preprod gateway, and no provider_admin_token credential channel is declared in any preprod profile auth.header_env. Remote preprod execution of this slice is unsupported by design, not by missing effort.
documented_gaps.OWNED_LOCAL_PROVIDER_BOT_OWNER_EDGE_DRIF: Live owned-runtime replay on the current dev binary (first attempted 2026-10-30 against apps/bcs/target/debug/bcs, binary sha256 dcbc39f07cedb62c8764987caa9fb05983dd7b3b1e6185022281cf0daa73d8d3) blocks at story request 8: PUT /bots/{bot_uuid}/visibility answered 403 "owner or manager role required for bot bot_..." and GET /bots/{bot_uuid} answered 403 "Not authorized to access bot". Provider Bot registration records created_by but never seeds bcs-edge-permission owner/manager edges, and POST /me/ensure-human backfills only list_legacy_bots_for_owner (legacy registration path), so the minting Human never gains an authority role over provider-registered Bots. The upstream story was frozen at f181ba44 (2026-10-22, provider-scoped owner collaboration #2654) and predates the bot-authority model c6f001209 (2026-10-27, #2625) that made these surfaces require authority edges. The frozen map stays unmodified; the drift is recorded here and the slice stays LOCAL_EXECUTOR_ONLY BLOCKED until a reviewed product decision re-scopes either the seeding contract or the story.
documented_gaps.WORKBENCH_WS_MOCK_ADMISSION: The Workbench WebSocket 101 upgrade and the owner/foreign connect projection boundary depend on loopback X-Mock-User-Id admission available only on the owned-local runtime; no preprod Workbench WebSocket evidence is claimed by this slice.

adaptability.blocker: The Provider registration/admin face is absent from the preprod public-v1 route bindings and no provider_admin_token credential channel exists there (PREPROD_PROVIDER_ADMIN_FACE_ABSENT), and the owned-local live replay currently blocks because provider-registered Bots receive no authority owner edges (OWNED_LOCAL_PROVIDER_BOT_OWNER_EDGE_DRIFT). Neither environment grants release credit.
